_note: pip install minihack (needs setuptools<81). Eating floor food is a TWO-step NetHack action: press LT (eat), then NetHack asks 'eat it? [ynq]' and you answer Y (yes). That confirm keystroke is why eating seems to 'freeze' after LT -- you must then press Y. (NetHack draws the prompt on the tty message line, which is NOT part of the pixel observation, so it can't be shown on screen; the LT-then-Y recipe in the instructions is what the player follows.) In NetHack y/n ARE the NW/SE movement keys, so the diagonal keys double as the yes/no answers (Y=act 7='y', X=act 5='n').
_keys_note: Discrete(85) full command set; we expose movement + eat. Compass 0-7 (0=N,1=E,2=S,3=W,4=NE,5=SE,6=SW,7=NW); 29=EAT. Arrows map to the cardinals, Y/A/B/X to the diagonals NW/NE/SW/SE, LT to eat. Y (act 7) sends keystroke 'y'='yes' and X (act 5) sends 'n'='no' at a [ynq] prompt. turn_based:true is required -- noop is action 0 (=move N). Keep the message Controls text in sync with 'keys' by hand.
_curriculum_note: Blocking: the block is this task played until completed (mode 'episode', n_episodes 1, advancing_outcomes ['won']); a death or the env's own step limit restarts the same level, and max_duration 300 s is the cap. ESC is the experimenter's way out.

text: You're hungry. Walk onto the food, then eat it in
two steps:  press  LT  to eat, then  Y  to confirm.
ARROWS       move  N / S / W / E
Y / A        move diagonally  NW / NE     (Y = 'yes')
B / X        move diagonally  SW / SE     (X = 'no')
LT  then  Y   eat the food you're standing on
